content.text:
Not completely. For a saved scalar setting, marking its key in `different_settings_to_system` does prevent the current preset from replacing that saved value during load. That would close the ordinary preset-default drift case. [Preset.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:2496) [PrintConfig.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:10133)

But “marked different” does **not** always mean “the project value wins.” Extruder-dependent vector settings still go through a merge: matched entries retain the saved values, while unmatched entries can come from the current preset. Missing settings are also filled from current defaults before that comparison. [PrintConfig.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:10142) [Config.hpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/Config.hpp:485)

So: **yes for the common saved-scalar substitution; no as a guarantee of exact version restoration.** I’d keep `different_settings_to_system` as an actual difference list and give version restore an explicit “saved values are authoritative” path. Blanket-marking keys also changes behavior elsewhere—for example, the 3MF loader uses this list to warn about modified G-code. [PresetBundle.cpp](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:2055)

which option will result in smaller upstream footprint:



- make the checking a key against different\_settings\_to\_system always return true.
- add all keys to =different\_settings\_to\_system at the end of the backup process
I’ll compare where each change would live and how far its effects would reach, including whether the backup-only option can stay inside JusPrin-owned code.

The second option has the smaller upstream footprint **if you apply it only to the autosave archive after export**. The capture flow is in JusPrin-owned `ProjectAutosave.cpp`: it exports `metadata.3mf`, then freezes the version, leaving a place to transform the pending archive without changing Orca-owned loading code. Implemented the backup-only option. New managed versions rewrite `metadata.3mf` so every setting saved in `project_settings.config` is listed in each `different_settings_to_system` group. Ordinary 3MF exports and Orca’s loader are unchanged. [Implementation](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:193)

The native harness verifies the saved key lists and successfully restores the checkpoint; the workspace unit suite passed (275 assertions). The full GUI harness still has one unrelated assertion failure, which I reproduced on the untouched checkout. [Regression test](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/c375/JusPrin/tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp:1327)

This closes the ordinary preset-default drift case, but it does not guarantee exact restoration of extruder-dependent vectors. The expanded lists may also produce a misleading modified-G-code warning on multi-filament restores; that path has not been runtime-tested.

I tested live capture and restore in the native macOS GUI harness. The disk increase is about 24% of each metadata archive, but only about 3.6–3.7 KB per checkpoint:

| Filament slots | Original backup | Managed checkpoint | Increase |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 15,085 B | 18,694 B | 3,609 B |
| 2 | 15,357 B | 19,103 B | 3,746 B |

At the 200-version limit, that’s roughly **0.7 MiB extra per project** for projects like this one. The separate mesh resource was unchanged. So the percentage is noticeable, but the absolute disk cost is small.

Both checkpoints restored successfully. The more important finding is a UX regression: restoring the two-filament checkpoint displayed a misleading **“Modified G-code”** warning. All new harness checks passed; the full harness still exits on one unrelated failure that I also reproduced on the untouched checkout.
